profile.name: Itsuki Kawamura

Handled routing, BGP and infrastructure troubleshooting.
Worked on an on-premises to AWS migration project.
Worked with VPC, EC2, Transit Gateway, Direct Connect and VPN connectivity.
Supported hybrid connectivity design and testing.
Created or worked with infrastructure design documents and test plans.

projects.name: AWS Windows Maintenance Automation
projects.summary: Automated maintenance workflow for a private Windows Server EC2 instance using AWS managed services.
implementation: EC2 has no public IP.
Administrative access uses AWS Systems Manager instead of RDP from the Internet.
Step Functions orchestrates stop, snapshot, start, patching, reboot, health checks and notifications.
EventBridge Scheduler triggers monthly maintenance.
Lambda performs patch scanning and starts the maintenance workflow when missing patches are detected.
Infrastructure is deployed with Terraform.
GitHub Actions uses AWS OIDC for CI/CD.
A manual destroy workflow is included.
validation: Successfully tested the normal maintenance workflow.
Tested failure handling by intentionally using an invalid Windows service name.
Confirmed automatic EventBridge Scheduler to Step Functions execution.

projects.name: Azure Private Infrastructure with Terraform
projects.summary: Private Azure VM infrastructure demonstrating Terraform, Managed Identity and private access to Azure Storage.
implementation: The VM has no public IP.
Inbound SSH is disabled.
Password authentication is disabled.
Storage public network access is disabled.
Storage is accessed through a Private Endpoint.
Private DNS is configured with privatelink.blob.core.windows.net.
The VM uses a system-assigned Managed Identity.
The identity is granted Storage Blob Data Reader.
Terraform state is stored remotely in Azure Storage using Microsoft Entra authentication.
GitHub Actions uses OIDC authentication to Azure.
validation: Confirmed that write access fails when the Managed Identity only has Storage Blob Data Reader.
Temporarily granted Contributor permissions for a write test.
Returned the identity to Reader permissions.

projects.name: AWS Private Application Infrastructure
projects.summary: Private EC2 application infrastructure deployed with Terraform and configured with Ansible through AWS Systems Manager.
implementation: EC2 has no public IP.
No inbound SSH is allowed.
The Application Load Balancer accepts Internet traffic.
The EC2 Security Group allows TCP 80 only from the ALB Security Group.
Ansible connects through amazon.aws.aws_ssm.
Docker and nginx are configured by Ansible.
Terraform provisions the AWS infrastructure.
GitHub Actions orchestrates Terraform and configuration automation.
validation: Confirmed end-to-end Internet to ALB to private EC2 to Docker nginx connectivity.

projects.name: AWS Terraform CI/CD with GitHub OIDC
projects.summary: Terraform CI/CD pipeline using GitHub Actions and AWS OIDC without long-lived AWS access keys.
implementation: GitHub Actions authenticates to AWS using OIDC.
Terraform runs format, initialization, validation, plan and apply stages.
Terraform state is stored remotely in S3.
S3 versioning is enabled for the state bucket.
Terraform S3 native state locking is used.
The AWS trust policy restricts GitHub OIDC subject claims.
lessons_learned: GitHub-hosted runners are ephemeral, so local Terraform state cannot be relied on across workflow runs.
Remote Terraform state is required for repeatable CI/CD deployments.
Recent GitHub repositories may use immutable repository identifiers in OIDC subject claims.

projects.name: AWS Private EC2 with Systems Manager
projects.summary: Private EC2 infrastructure managed through AWS Systems Manager without inbound administrative access.
implementation: Private Amazon Linux EC2 instance.
No inbound Security Group rules.
Systems Manager VPC endpoints.
Encrypted gp3 storage.
IMDSv2 enabled.
IAM role using AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore.
NAT Gateway can provide optional general Internet access.

projects.name: AWS CloudWatch Alarm and SNS
projects.summary: Infrastructure monitoring example using EC2 status checks, CloudWatch Alarms and SNS notifications.
implementation: CloudWatch monitors EC2 StatusCheckFailed.
SNS delivers email notifications.
Infrastructure is provisioned with Terraform.
validation: Used CloudWatch alarm state modification to validate the notification path.
The test validated CloudWatch to SNS notification behavior rather than a real EC2 infrastructure failure.
